theme: 3 terms for charts in SwiftUI: the chart view, the bar element and the trend element

terms.definition: A view from the Charts framework that draws your data as marks.
terms.example: Put the steps into a Chart on the home screen.
terms.code:
let steps = [3, 5, 4]
Chart(steps, id: \.self) { n in
    BarMark(x: .value("N", n), y: .value("V", n))
}

terms.definition: A mark that draws one bar for a value, for example steps per day.
terms.example: Use a BarMark for each day.

terms.definition: A mark that connects values with a line, to show a trend over time.
terms.example: Switch to a LineMark to show the trend.

Today's terms
Chart - A view from the Charts framework that draws your data as marks.
BarMark - A mark that draws one bar for a value, for example steps per day.
LineMark - A mark that connects values with a line, to show a trend over time.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Chart, BarMark and LineMark in English?

dialogue.title: Daily steps chart

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the product owner wants a graph of daily steps.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Import the Charts framework, and use a Chart. It draws your data as marks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do I need a third-party package?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. Chart is part of Apple's Charts framework.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do I show one bar for every day?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add a BarMark. It draws one bar for a value, like steps per day.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In the code, `x` and `y` are both `n`. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Only for a test. In a real app, `x` is the day and `y` is the steps.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now the owner wants a trend line, not bars.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a LineMark. It connects the values with a line, so you see the trend.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I use a BarMark and a LineMark together?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A Chart can hold many marks. Just keep it readable.

dialogue.code:
let steps = [3, 5, 4]
Chart(steps, id: \.self) { n in
    BarMark(x: .value("N", n), y: .value("V", n))
    LineMark(x: .value("N", n), y: .value("V", n))
}
